newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends mixed on Tokyo trends.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends mixed on Tokyo trends.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended mixed in tandem with uncertainties in Tokyo and lack of buying interest at home, traders said.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted market indicator price for November RSS 1 buyer at 309.5 cents ($1.23) a kg, down one cent from Friday. November SMR 20 buyer was unchanged at 306 cents.
Trading houses quoted midday offer levels, with the SMR 20 going for 304 cents a kg, SMR10 at 305, SMR 5 at 316, SMR L at 342, SMR CV at 362 and drum latex at 232 to 234 cents.
"The market was basically unchanged from morning," said a dealer. "There was not much buying interest as the U.S. is on a public holiday and the Far East was staying quiet."

Traders said with the absence of leads, the market followed the mixed trends in Tokyo. The continuance of rain this week might help prices rebound if rubber tapping and stocks in the market were affected, they said.
The INRO five-day average fell to 238.87 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Oct 11 from 238.94 on Oct 10. The daily indicator was at 239.35 from 239.53 previously.
